title: Including Input from Singaporeans Who Graduated Overseas in Fresh Graduates Employment Data
what_it_is: Including Input from Singaporeans Who Graduated Overseas in Fresh Graduates Employment Data

sections.label: Graduate underemployment and employment rates
sections.summary: Resident graduates aged 25 to 29 from overseas universities had a 0.8% underemployment rate in 2025, slightly above the 0.7% for local autonomous university graduates, with around nine in 10 employed.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Based on the internationally recognised measure of time-related underemployment, which refers to part-time workers who prefer full-time employment, the underemployment rate among residents aged 25 to 29 who graduated from overseas universities was 0.8% in 2025.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: This is about 0.1%, slightly above the 0.7% recorded for graduates from local autonomous universities.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Overall, the employment outcomes for graduates aged 25 to 29, remain generally strong for both local autonomous universities and overseas universities graduates, with around nine in 10 employed.

sections.label: Graduate employment rate differential
sections.summary: In 2025, employment rates for local autonomous universities and overseas universities graduates were above 90%, with a differential of just slightly over 1%.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: What we have seen from last year, which I want to share with Members, from the employment rate in 2025, the local autonomous universities graduates, as well as the overseas universities graduates, employment rate was at above 90%.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: The differential between overseas universities graduates versus the local autonomous universities graduates is just slightly over 1%.

sections.label: Total employment growth 2025
sections.summary: Total employment growth for 2025 was about 57,300, stronger than the about 44,500 in 2024.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: For the entire year, for 2025, the total employment growth, which is about 57,300, was stronger than a year ago, in 2024, which was about 44,500.

sections.label: Firms' hiring and wage expectations
sections.summary: The share of firms expecting to hire in the next three months edged down from 44% in September 2025 to 43% in December 2025, while those expecting to raise wages rose from 19% to about 26%.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Another slight note of optimism, the share of firms expecting to hire in the next three months only edged down slightly – from 44% in September 2025, to 43% in December 2025.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: But if you compare this at the same time, a larger share of firms expects to raise wages over the same period, rising from 19% to about 26%.
